As used in this Form 10-K, "MetLife," the "Company," "we," "our" and "us" refer to MetLife, Inc., a Delaware corporation incorporated in 1999, its subsidiaries and affiliates.

MetLife is one of the world's leading financial services companies, providing insurance, annuities, employee benefits and asset management. We hold leading market positions in the United States ("U.S."), Asia, Latin America, Europe and the Middle East. We are also one of the largest institutional investors in the U.S. with a general account portfolio invested primarily in fixed income securities (corporate, structured products, municipals, and government and agency) and mortgage loans, as well as real estate, real estate joint ventures ("REJVs"), other limited partnerships and equity securities.

We believe that our trusted global brand, diversified and resilient business, and position as a leader in attractive markets are the powers of our business. Over the next four years we will continue to execute on our New Frontier strategy, which was designed to accelerate growth across our global platform while delivering attractive returns and all-weather performance. New Frontier builds upon the success of our Next Horizon strategy, which we implemented in 2019, with an aim to focus, simplify and differentiate the Company.
Under our New Frontier strategy, we intend to leverage the Company's strengths to prioritize growth across four key areas of opportunity:
•Extend our leadership in Group Benefits; •Capitalize on our unique retirement platform; •Accelerate our growth in asset management; and
•Expand in high growth international markets.

In the fourth quarter of 2025, MetLife executed a reorganization to align with its strategic initiative to accelerate growth in asset management. As part of this reorganization, the Company adjusted its segment structure. MetLife Investment Management, the Company's institutional asset management business ("MIM"), which was previously reported in Corporate & Other, became a reportable segment. MetLife Holdings was removed as a reportable segment, and its business is now primarily reported in Corporate & Other. These changes were applied retrospectively for all years presented. Additionally, certain products formerly reported in MetLife Holdings have been moved to Group Benefits and Retirement and Income Solutions ("RIS"). This change was applied only for the year ended December 31, 2025. The foregoing changes did not impact prior period consolidated net income (loss) or consolidated adjusted earnings, and are collectively referred to as the "Strategic Reorganization." As a result of the Strategic Reorganization, MetLife is organized into the following six segments: Group Benefits; RIS; Asia; Latin America; Europe, the Middle East and Africa ("EMEA"); and MIM. In addition, the Company continues to report certain of its results of operations in Corporate & Other. See "— Segments and Corporate & Other" and Note 2 of the Notes to the Consolidated Financial Statements for further information on the Company's segments and Corporate & Other.

We offer a broad range of products and services aimed at serving the financial needs of our customers. We sell these products to corporations and other institutions (including local, state and federal governments) and their respective employees, as well as individuals.
We have built a leading position in the U.S. group insurance market through long-standing relationships with many of the largest employers in the U.S.

Our Group Benefits segment, based in the U.S., offers life insurance, dental, group short- and long-term disability, paid family and medical leave, individual disability, accidental death and dismemberment ("AD&D") insurance, accident & health insurance, and vision, as well as prepaid legal plans and pet insurance. We also sell administrative services-only ("ASO") arrangements to some employers.

We distribute Group Benefits products and services through a sales force primarily comprised of MetLife employees that is segmented by the size of the target customer. Account executives sell either directly to corporate and other group customers or through an intermediary, such as a broker or consultant. Employers have been emphasizing voluntary products and, as a result, we have increased our focus on communicating and marketing to employees in order to further foster sales of those products.

We have entered into arrangements with third parties to expand opportunities to market and distribute Group Benefits products and services. We also sell Group Benefits products and services through sponsoring associations and affinity groups and provide life, dental, accident & health, and vision coverage to certain employees of the U.S. Government. We have longstanding relationships with these employees and continue to cultivate and expand them through additional product offerings.

paragraphs: Any or each of the events described below may (or may continue to) adversely affect the global economy or global financial markets, or our reputation, regulatory, customer, or other relationships, results of operations, liquidity or cash flows, statutory capital position, ability to meet our obligations, credit and financial strength ratings, financial condition, or the market price of our common stock. The effects may vary depending on timing, product, market, region or segment.

Many of these risks are interrelated and could occur under similar business and economic conditions, and the occurrence of any of them may cause others to emerge or worsen. Such combinations could materially increase the severity of the cumulative or separate impact of these risks.

These risk factors do not describe all potential risks that could affect MetLife. You should carefully consider the risk factors together with other information contained in this Annual Report on Form 10-K, including "Business," "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" and the consolidated financial statements and accompanying notes in "Financial Statements and Supplementary Data," and other reports and materials MetLife submits to the SEC.

Market factors, including interest rates, credit spreads, declining equity or debt markets, derivative prices and availability, real estate conditions, foreign currency exchange rates, consumer and government spending, government default or spending reductions to avoid default, business investment, climate change, public health risks, volatility, disruptions and strength of the capital markets, deflation and inflation, and government actions in response thereto, may inhibit revenue growth, reduce investment opportunities and result in reduced investment returns or losses, derivative losses, reductions in fees generated, changes in insurance liabilities, impairments, increased valuation allowances, increases in reserves, reduced net investment income and changes in unrealized gain or loss positions.

Market conditions resulting in reductions in the value of assets we manage or lower transaction volume may have an adverse effect on the revenues and profitability of our institutional asset management services, which depend on fees related primarily to the value of assets under management ("AUM").

Higher unemployment, changes to inflation, lower family income, lower corporate earnings, greater government regulation, lower business investment, lower consumer spending, elevated incidence of claims, adverse utilization of benefits relative to our best estimate expectations, lapses or surrenders of policies, reduced demand for our products and services, and deferred or canceled payments of insurance premiums may negatively affect our earnings and capitalization.

MetLife is one of the world's leading financial services companies, providing insurance, annuities, employee benefits and asset management. In the fourth quarter of 2025, MetLife completed the Strategic Reorganization. As a result, MetLife is organized into the following six segments: Group Benefits; RIS; Asia; Latin America; EMEA; and MIM. Our outlook reflects continued uncertainty around inflation and unemployment in 2026. We expect the U.S. dollar to remain relatively stable in 2026 compared to 2025.

Based on the forward yield curve as of December 31, 2025, we expect long-term interest rates to moderately rise in 2026 with the yield curve steepening, as short-term interest rates decline. We believe that our investment portfolio is highly diversified and positioned to perform well in a variety of economic scenarios. See "— Industry Trends — Impact of Market Interest Rates" for discussion of the mitigating actions the Company has taken to reduce interest rate sensitivity, as market interest rates are a key driver of our results.

As of December 31, 2025, we had $3.6 billion of cash and liquid assets at the holding companies which is within our $3.0 billion to $4.0 billion holding company cash target. In 2026, we expect to maintain this holding company cash target. We also returned a total of approximately $4.4 billion to shareholders in 2025, and we remain on track to generate approximately $25.0 billion in free cash flow over the five-year period of 2025 to 2029.

Our continued capital stress testing and longstanding commitment to liquidity position us to withstand a variety of economic conditions. We do not expect any material liquidity deficiencies, and we expect to remain able to comply with the financial covenants of our credit agreements. See "— Liquidity and Capital Resources." We will continue reviewing accounting estimates, asset valuations and various financial scenarios for capital and liquidity implications. See "— Investments — Current Environment" and "Risk Factors" for additional information.

Assuming (i) interest rates follow the observable forward yield curves as of December 31, 2025, including a 10-year U.S. Treasury rate of 4.40% at December 31, 2026, (ii) S&P 500 equity index annual return of 5%, and (iii) private equity annual returns of 9% in 2026 which would contribute to $1.6 billion (pre-tax) of total estimated variable investment income for full year 2026; we expect to maintain the two-year average annual ratio of free cash flow to adjusted earnings, excluding total notable items, at 65% to 75%.

Further, based on the aforementioned assumptions, we are maintaining our near-term annual targets for (i) adjusted return on equity, excluding total notable items, of 15%-17%, and (ii) double-digit adjusted earnings per share growth, excluding total notable items.

在本Form 10-K中，"MetLife," "the Company," "we," "our" 和 "us" 指的是MetLife, Inc., 一家於1999年成立的特拉華州公司，其子公司及附屬機構。
MetLife是全球領先的金融服務公司之一，提供保險、年金、員工福利及資產管理服務。我們在美國（"U.S."）、亞洲、拉丁美洲、歐洲及中東地區擁有領先的市場地位。我們也是美國最大的機構投資者之一，持有以固定收益證券（企業債、結構性產品、市政債、政府及機構債券）及房貸貸款為主的總帳戶投資組合，以及不動產、不動產合資企業（"REJVs"）、其他有限合夥企業及股權證券。
我們相信，我們受信任的全球品牌、多元化且具韌性的業務，以及在具吸引力市場中領導者的地位，是我們業務的動力。在接下來的四年中，我們將持續執行我們的New Frontier策略，該策略旨在加速我們全球平台的成長，同時提供有吸引力的回報及全年無休的表現。New Frontier策略建立在我們2019年實施的Next Horizon策略的成功基礎上，目標是聚焦、簡化並區隔本公司。
根據我們的New Frontier策略，我們意圖利用本公司的優勢，優先在四大成長機會領域推動成長：
•擴展我們在團體福利領域的領導地位；•善用我們獨特的退休平台；•加速我們在資產管理領域的成長；以及
•擴展至高成長國際市場。

於2025年第四季，MetLife執行了一項重整，以配合其戰略計畫，加速在資產管理領域的成長。此重整作業中，本公司調整了其應報告分部結構。MetLife Investment Management，本公司之機構資產管理業務（"MIM"），先前歸屬於Corporate & Other，現已成為應報告分部。MetLife Holdings不再作為應報告分部，其業務現已主要歸屬於Corporate & Other。此等變更已對所有列示年份追溯應用。此外，某些先前歸屬於MetLife Holdings之產品已移至Group Benefits and Retirement and Income Solutions（"RIS"）。此變更僅適用於2025年12月31日結算年度。上述變更未影響往期合併淨損益（損失）或合併調整後盈餘，且 collectively referred to as the "Strategic Reorganization." 因此，MetLife現已組織為以下六個應報告分部：Group Benefits；RIS；Asia；Latin America；Europe, the Middle East and Africa（"EMEA"）；以及MIM。此外，本公司繼續於Corporate & Other中報告部分營運成果。請參閱 "— Segments and Corporate & Other" 以及財務會計彙編附註第2項，以取得更多關於本公司應報告分部及Corporate & Other之資訊。
我們提供廣泛的產品與服務，以滿足客戶的財務需求。我們將這些產品銷售給公司及其他機構（包括地方政府、州政府及聯邦政府）及其相關員工，以及個人。
我們透過與許多美國最大僱主的長期關係，在美國團體保險市場建立了領導地位。
我們的Group Benefits分部，位於美國，提供人壽保險、牙科保險、團體短期及長期失能保險、有薪家庭及醫療假、個人失能、意外死亡及肢體喪失（"AD&D"）保險、意外及健康保險，以及視力保險，以及預付法律服務計畫及寵物保險。我們也向部分僱主銷售僅提供行政服務（"ASO"）的安排。
我們透過銷售團隊銷售Group Benefits產品與服務，該銷售團隊主要由MetLife員工組成，並根據目標客戶規模進行分區。帳戶經理直接向公司及其他團體客戶銷售，或透過中介，例如經紀人或顧問。僱主已越來越重視自願性產品，因此我們已增加對員工的溝通與行銷，以進一步促進這些產品的銷售。
我們已與第三方簽訂協議，以擴大行銷與分佈Group Benefits產品與服務的機會。我們也透過贊助協會及親近羣體銷售Group Benefits產品與服務，並為美國政府某些員工提供人壽、牙科、意外及健康及視力保險。我們與這些員工有長期關係，並持續透過增加產品選擇來培養與擴展這些關係。

MetLife為全球領先之金融服務公司，提供保險、年金、員工福利及資產管理服務。在2025年第四季，MetLife完成戰略重整。因此，MetLife已組織為以下六個應報告分部：羣組福利；RIS；亞洲；拉丁美洲；EMEA；以及MIM。此外，公司持續於企業及其他部門報告部分運作結果。請參閱"商業—分部與企業及其他"及合併財務報表附註第2項，以取得公司分部與企業及其他之更多資訊。
我們的展望反映2026年通貨膨脹與失業率持續不確定性。我們預期2026年美國美元相較於2025年將維持相對穩定。
根據2025年12月31日的前向殖利率曲線，我們預期2026年長期利率將溫和上漲，殖利率曲線將趨於陡峭，因短端利率下降。我們認為本公司投資組合高度分散，並能適應多種經濟情境表現良好。請參閱「— 行業趨勢 — 市場利率的影響」以瞭解本公司為降低利率敏感度所採取的緩衝措施，因市場利率是影響我們結果的關鍵因素。
截至2025年12月31日，本公司持有公司持有約36億美元現金及流動資產，符合本公司持有公司現金目標30億至40億美元。2026年，我們預期將維持此持有公司現金目標。我們也在2025年回饋約44億美元給股東，並預期在2025至2029年這五年的期間內產生約250億美元的自由現金流。
我們持續進行資本壓力測試及長期重視流動性，使我們能承受多種經濟情境。我們不預期會有任何重大流動性不足，且預期將能遵守信用協議的財務約束條款。請參閱「— 流動性及資本資源」。我們將持續審查會計估計、資產評價及各種財務情境對資本及流動性的影響。請參閱「— 投資 — 當前環境」及「風險因素」以取得更多資訊。
假設（i）利率遵循2025年12月31日的可觀察前向殖利率曲線，包括2026年12月31日10年期美國國庫券利率為4.40%，（ii）S&P 500股價指數年回報率為5%，以及（iii）2026年私人股權年回報率為9%，這將貢獻約16億美元（稅前）的總預估變動投資收入，用以全年2026年；我們預期將維持自由現金流與調整後營收的兩年平均年比率，排除總重要項目後，維持在65%至75%之間。
進一步地，根據上述假設，我們維持我們的短期年度目標為（i）排除總重要項目後的調整後股東權益回報率為15%-17%，以及（ii）排除總重要項目後的雙位數調整後每股盈餘成長。

paragraphs: 任何或各項下列所述事件，可能（或持續）對全球經濟或全球金融市場，或本公司聲譽、監管、客戶或其他關係、營運成果、流動性或現金流、法定資本狀況、履行義務的能力、信用與財務強度評級、財務狀況或本公司普通股的市價產生不利影響。影響程度可能因時間、產品、市場、地區或分部而有所不同。
許多這些風險彼此相關，可能在相似的營運與經濟條件下發生，且其中一項事件的發生可能導致其他事件出現或情況惡化。這些組合可能顯著增加這些風險的總體或個別影響程度。
這些風險因素並未涵蓋所有可能影響MetLife的潛在風險。您應仔細考量這些風險因素，並與本年度報告表10-K中包含的其他資訊一併審閱，包括「業務」、「管理層對財務狀況與營運成果之討論與分析」以及「財務報表與補充資料」中之合併財務報表與附註，以及其他MetLife提交至SEC的報告與資料。

市場因素，包括利率、信用 spreads、股權或債務市場下跌、衍生性商品價格與可取得性、房地產狀況、外幣交換率、消費者與政府支出、政府違約或為避免違約而減少支出、企業投資、氣候變遷、公共衛生風險、波動性、中斷與資本市場的強度、通貨緊縮與通貨膨脹，以及政府對此所採取的行動，可能抑制收入成長、減少投資機會，並導致投資回報減少或損失、衍生性商品損失、產生費用減少、保險責任變動、減損、增加撥備、增加準備金、淨投資收入減少以及未實現損益位置變動。
因市場條件導致所管理資產價值下降或交易量減少，可能對我們的機構資產管理服務收入與利潤產生不利影響，這些服務收入主要取決於所管理資產價值（"AUM"）相關的費用。
失業率上升、通貨膨脹變動、家庭收入下降、企業獲利減少、政府監管增加、企業投資減少、消費者支出減少、聲請案件發生率增加、保險福利使用率相對於本公司最佳預估期望值表現不佳、保單中止或解約、我們產品與服務需求減少，以及保險 premiums 延後或取消支付，可能對本公司獲利與資本結構產生負面影響。
